guarantees.claim: For each bit index k from 0 to 31, perm_data[k] equals data[perm_sel[k]].

formal.consequent: forall (int k=0; k<32; k++) perm_data[k] == data[perm_sel[k]]

formal_sketch.consequent: forall (int k=0; k<32; k++) perm_data[k] == data[perm_sel[k]]

guarantees.claim: Bits perm_data[RandWidth-1:32] are not assigned, resulting in unknown (X) values.

formal_sketch.consequent: Bits perm_data[RandWidth-1:32] are not assigned, resulting in unknown (X) values

assumptions.claim: Parameter RandWidth must be >= 32 to avoid illegal index into return variable.
assumptions.risk: If RandWidth < 32, assignment to perm_data[k] for k >= 32 causes out-of-bounds access, leading to compile/elaboration error.

assumptions.claim: Each element of perm_sel (indices 0..31) must be a valid bit index into data, i.e., 0 <= perm_sel[k] < RandWidth.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-range perm_sel would access data bits beyond its defined range, yielding X or synthesis don't-care, potentially corrupting integrity of permuted output.

formal.consequent: forall (int k=0; k<32; k++) (0 <= perm_sel[k] && perm_sel[k] < RandWidth)

formal_sketch.consequent: forall (int k=0; k<32; k++) (0 <= perm_sel[k] && perm_sel[k] < RandWidth)

uncertain_points.claim: The function requires RandWidth >= 32; if a top-level configuration sets RandWidth < 32, the design will not compile.
uncertain_points.risk: Failure to compile may mask integration errors or cause redesign later.

formal_sketch.consequent: The function requires RandWidth >= 32; if a top-level configuration sets RandWidth < 32, the design will not compile

uncertain_points.claim: When RandWidth > 32, the function leaves bits 32..RandWidth-1 of perm_data unassigned (X); if this data is used as a key, mask, or digest, the X bits could propagate or cause synthesis-dependent behavior, potentially leaking secret information.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven high bits may lead to non-deterministic hardware that weakens masking or key integrity.

formal_sketch.consequent: the function leaves bits 32..RandWidth-1 of perm_data unassigned (X); if this data is used as a key, mask, or digest, the X bits could propagate or cause synthesis-dependent behavior, potentially leaking secret information

security_implications: Permutation of data likely used in key manager for masking or secret derivation. If RandWidth > 32, the unassigned upper bits of perm_data may be X, leading to potential secret leakage or corruption. Out-of-range perm_sel accesses could read unintended data bits, possibly exposing internal state.
